name: Tower Hamlets

applications.description: Redevelopment of the Site to provide a four storey building comprising 9 no. self-contained residential flats (Use class C3), including 1 no. M4(3) unit, along with soft and hard landscaping.

game.plainAsk: Knock the site down and put up a 4-storey block of 9 flats. None of them are affordable, and one is built for a wheelchair user.
game.plainImpact: Nine extra homes, but 0% affordable (London Plan asks 35% on bigger schemes). This is under 10 homes so they dodge the usual affordable rule. Neighbours get a new block; people on the 3,096 temporary-accommodation list get nothing from this one.

applications.description: Demolition of existing building. Erection of part 8, part 7 and part 6-storey building comprising residential units (Use Class C3) and commercial space (Flexible Use Class E/Sui Generis [Recording Studio]), with associated amenity and play space, accessible car parking, cycle parking, landscaping, changes to existing access points and other associated works.

game.plainAsk: Knock the building down and put up a part-8, part-7, part-6 storey block of homes, plus shops, offices and a recording studio, with play space.
game.plainImpact: A major in Wapping (36 homes on the desk, 20% affordable vs London Plan 35%). St Paul's Whitechapel school is within 400 m; Royal London is in the 400–1,200 m sweet spot. The 3,096 get a thin slice if that 20% is real.

place.schoolName: St Paul's Whitechapel Church of England Primary School

applications.description: Demolition of existing buildings and redevelopment of the site to provide a residential development, comprising 65 dwellings, plus disabled car parking spaces, cycle parking, refuse/recycling facilities and access together with landscaping including communal and private amenity space, and associated development.Minor Material Amendments to Planning permission Ref: PA/21/02746, Dated 09/12/2022: Amendments include: Change the tenure of unit C.01 from Affordable Rented to Private. Change Units A09 and A10 (currently both 2 bed units) to 1x1B and 1x3B.
applications.site_name: Langdon Park Community Centre And Land At Rear, St Leonards Road, London

game.plainAsk: They already have permission for 65 homes. They want to change the deal: one affordable-rent home becomes a private home, and two 2-beds become a 1-bed and a 3-bed.
game.plainImpact: Net affordable homes go down by one on a 65-home site. This sits in the Langdon Park conservation area, next to a listed war memorial. Langdon Park school is on the doorstep (about 40 m).

applications.description: Comprehensive redevelopment of the site comprising demolition of existing buildings (with the exception of the PDC Building, including partial demolition thereof), and the erection of a 5-storey building to provide residential dwellings (Use Class C3) and an Idea Store (Use Class F1), alongside associated servicing, car parking, public realm and ancillary works.
applications.site_name: Professional Development Centre, 229 Bethnal Green Road, E2 6AB And 10 Turin Street, E2 6GX

game.plainAsk: Knock most of the training centre (keep the PDC building, partly stripped). Put up a 5-storey block of homes and a new Idea Store — a library / learning space.
game.plainImpact: A major (30 homes on the desk, 20% affordable vs London Plan 35%). Mulberry Academy Shoreditch is within 400 m; Royal London is in the 400–1,200 m sweet spot. The Idea Store is the public bit; the 3,096 still need those affordable homes to be real.

applications.description: Residential development of Bow Wharf to provide 66 residential properties incorporating single new commercial unit through the conversion of the existing warehouse building and construction of two new apartment blocks following the demolition of existing structures, together with the provision of an altered vehicular access to Wennington Road and associated landscaping and play spaces.
applications.site_name: Land at Bow Wharf, Grove Road, London, E3

game.plainAsk: Knock the extra structures, keep and convert the warehouse, and add two new blocks: 66 homes plus one shop or office, with play space, on the canal.
game.plainImpact: Sixty-six homes, 20% affordable vs London Plan 35%. This sits in the Regent's Canal conservation area. Chisenhale Primary is within 400 m; Mile End Hospital is in the 400–1,200 m sweet spot. A 66-home scheme under 35% is a real gap vs the 432-a-year target.

applications.description: Demolition of existing structures and buildings, not including the Boiler House and Cooperage buildings which will be refurbished.  Construction of five new buildings comprising approximately 35,000sqm GIA of Residential, Office, Retail, Food & Beverage, Community use, Supermarket, Microbrewery, Market space, Event space and Public Toilets of Use Classes E (a), (b), and (g), Use Class F1, F2, Sui Generis, and Use Class C3, reaching a maximum height of approximately 29m (42.78 AOD) Block O - The Boiler House: To be retained and refurbished with a new extension to the east and a viewing platform.  To provide event and exhibition space. (Use Class F1)Blocks 3A and 3B - on Buxton Street.  Construction of new buildings part 2/part 3/part 6/part 8 storeys with a maximum height of approximately 29m.   To provide food and drink, cinema/event space and public toilets (use classes E(b) and sui generis) at ground floor and office (use class E(g)(i) on upper floors.Block K - The Cooperage building - on Spital Street.  Retention and refurbishment.  To provide event space and microbrewery at ground floor (use classes Sui generis) and retention of existing art studio space at first floor. (Use class E(g)(iii)).Block 1 - on Spital Street.  Construction of a new building part single/part 3 storeys.  To provide retail (Use class E(a)) at ground floor and office floor space (use class E(g)(i)) on upper floors.Block 2 - Construction of a new 7-storey building, with a maximum height of approximately 29m.  To provide a market space (Use class E) and public toilets (Sui Generis) at ground floor and office space (Use class E(g)(i)) on upper floors.Block J - Demolition of the existing cash and carry building on Spital Street, Woodseer Street and Hanbury Street. Construction of a new part 4/part 5/part 7-storey building, with a maximum height of approximately 27m.  To provide retail floorspace (Use class E(a)) at ground floor.  On upper floors 44 new homes (Use class C3) fronting Spital Street and Hanbury Street.   Office space (Use class E(g)(i) fronting Woodseer Street.Provision of new publicly accessible routes through the site from Brick Lane, Buxton Street and Spital Street, landscaping, a vehicle and servicing loading bay, and two new publicly accessible squares.This application is accompanied by an Environmental Impact Assessment. (EIA).
applications.site_name: Truman's Brewery, Land fronting Brick Lane, Buxton Street, Spital Street, Woodseer Street and Hanbury Street, E1

game.plainAsk: Keep the old Boiler House and Cooperage; knock the rest. Build shops, offices, a cinema, a microbrewery, a market, and 44 new homes in a block up to 7 storeys on Brick Lane.
game.plainImpact: Forty-four homes at 20% affordable vs London Plan 35%, inside the Fournier Street conservation area, on the listed Black Eagle Brewery site. St Anne's and Guardian Angels school is within 400 m; Royal London is in the 400–1,200 m sweet spot. This is a big heritage fight.

place.schoolName: St Anne's and Guardian Angels Catholic Primary School

applications.description: Redevelopment of the site comprising the demolition of existing buildings (including Harriot House, Apsley House, Pattison House, The Redcoat Centre and Redcoat Community Centre) to provide 407 residential units (Class C3) across buildings ranging in height from 4-8 storeys and community centre building of 1,167m2 GIA (Class E (e-f), Class F1 (e-f), Class F.2 (b)), together with associated landscaped communal amenity space, accessible car parking, secure cycle parking spaces and refuse/recycling storage facilities.
applications.site_name: Land Comprising Harriott House, Apsley House, Pattison House, The Redcoat Centre & Redcoat Community Centre, London, E1

game.plainAsk: Knock down Harriott House, Apsley House, Pattison House, the Redcoat Centre and the community centre. Put up 407 homes in blocks of 4 to 8 storeys, plus a new community centre.
game.plainImpact: This is an estate rebuild. 407 homes at 20% affordable vs London Plan 35%. Missing 35% on 407 homes is a big hole vs the 432-a-year target. Existing residents get demolished first. Bishop Challoner school is within 400 m; Royal London is in the 400–1,200 m sweet spot.

applications.description: Variation of Condition 2 of planning permission PA/23/02375 to increase the number of private homes and reduce the number of affordable homes, reconfigure internal layouts and external elevations.The description of development of permission PA/23/02375 is as follows: 'Comprehensive and phased mixed-use redevelopment comprising 1,358 residential units (Class C3), secondary school (Class F), commercial, business and services E(a)-E(g)(i), community uses (Class F), police base (sui generis) car and cycle basement parking, associated landscaping, new public realm and all other necessary enabling works.This application is accompanied by an Environmental Statement.'
applications.site_name: Former Westferry Printworks, 235 Westferry Road, London, E14

game.plainAsk: They already have permission. They want to change it: MORE private flats, FEWER affordable ones, in a huge Isle of Dogs scheme (1,358 homes on the books).
game.plainImpact: This is the big one. Cutting affordable homes on a 1,358-home site moves the borough backwards vs the 432-a-year affordable target. House prices/rents get a luxury bump. Luxury bumps prices; renters get squeezed.
